item.title: Dogashima Sea Caves: West Izu's Skylight Grotto and Boat Tours — Guide
item.description: Dogashima, on the Izu Peninsula’s wild west coast, is famous for its white volcanic tuff cliffs and wave-carved sea caves, the striking result of layered volcanic ash sculpted by the sea. The highlight is Tensodo, a skylight cave whose roof has collapsed to leave a natural round opening, sending a shaft of light onto the blue-green water below; small sightseeing boats cruise into the cave itself, while a clifftop path above lets you peer down through the skylight, and at low tide a tombolo land bridge appears to a nearby island.

item.title: Goishi Coast: Iwate's Pine-Shaded Rocky Shore — Guide
item.description: The Goishi Coast in Ofunato is a scenic stretch of the southern Sanriku shoreline — black pebble beaches (whose stones give the coast its ‘Go-stone’ name), wave-carved rock formations, and a pine-shaded coastal trail leading past thundering sea caves and blowholes. An easy, atmospheric walk on the recovering Sanriku coast. 🗓️ At a Glance Location Ofunato, Iwate Hours Trail always open (daylight best) Admission Free Time needed 1–2 hours Best time Spring–summer; clear days What to See Black pebble beaches and wave-carved rocks.

item.title: Boso Sea Kayaking Guide: Tours, Caves & Access
item.description: The clear, sheltered waters and rugged little coves of the southern Boso Peninsula make it one of the best places near Tokyo to try sea kayaking. Guided tours paddle out from spots around Tateyama and Minamiboso to explore turquoise coves, slip into sea caves, glide past rocky islets and, on calm days, peer down at fish and coral over the gunwale. Beginner-friendly tours with stable double kayaks and instruction make it accessible to first-timers and families, while the warm Kuroshio current keeps the water inviting from spring through autumn.
